champion: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum-like disorder with coagulation deficiency
ordered_diagnoses: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum-like disorder with coagulation deficiency

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive skin laxity with coalesced papules and loss of elasticity, primarily affecting flexural areas, with a long-standing history
salient_findings: Asymptomatic yellowish coalesced papules in flexural areas
Severe skin sagging with loss of elasticity
Thick and leathery skinfolds on the neck, axillae, inguinal regions, abdomen, and limbs
key_facts: 20-year history of progressive skin laxity
Asymptomatic yellowish coalesced papules developed in early childhood
Skin sagging occurred on the abdomen and spread extensively with developmental growth
No extracutaneous involvement
Born to healthy nonconsanguineous parents
Younger sister had the same skin symptoms
Low clotting activity of factor X (52.2%)
Prolonged prothrombin time (12.8 seconds)
Excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments in the reticular dermis on skin biopsy
Compound heterozygous sequence variation in GGCX gene

s4.champion: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum-like disorder with coagulation deficiency

raw.champion: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum-like disorder with coagulation deficiency
raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of progressive skin laxity, yellowish coalesced papules, and excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments are consistent with pseudoxanthoma elasticum, while the low clotting activity of factor X and prolonged prothrombin time suggest a coagulation deficiency, which is further supported by the compound heterozygous sequence variation in the GGCX gene.

rejected.label: GGCX deficiency
rejected.why: Too narrow, does not account for full spectrum of symptoms

rejected.label: Cutis laxa
rejected.why: Does not typically present with calcification of elastic fibers
